records.title: Conference-matrix MDS code conjecture
records.statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and let ${\mathbb C}$ be a code of length $p+1$ constructed from a generator matrix that is a conference matrix. **Conference-matrix MDS conjecture.** The code ${\mathbb C}$ is an MDS code of dimension $\frac{p+1}{2}$ and minimum Hamming distance $\frac{p+3}{2}$. This would give an MDS code with parameters determined by the rank of a conference matrix over ${\mathbb Z}_p$; the source provides no resolution of the claim.

records.title: The spectral characterization of geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups on trees
records.statement: Let $T$ and $T'$ be trees. Assume that they are simultaneously co-spectral, their complements are co-spectral, and their line graphs are co-spectral. **Geodesic-growth conjecture.** Then $T$ and $T'$ have the same geodesic growth, meaning that the associated right-angled Coxeter groups $G(T)$ and $G(T')$ have the same geodesic growth series. The conjecture asks whether these three spectral data determine geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees; the paper establishes examples supporting the question but does not resolve the general implication.

records.title: Starlikeness conjecture for Cassinian balls in starlike domains
records.statement: Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain that is starlike with respect to $x\in G$, and let $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ denote the Cassinian ball of radius $r$. **Starlikeness conjecture.** For every $r>0$, the ball $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ is starlike with respect to $x$. This is a proposed extension of convexity results to starlike domains, and the paper does not establish it.

records.title: The combinatorial injection conjecture for dominance order on compositions
records.statement:
Let $A,a,B,b$ be integers with $A \geq B \geq 0$ and $a \geq b \geq 0$. For $m,n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{U}^m_n$ denote the set of compositions of $n$ with $m$ non-negative parts. For compositions $\lambda$ and $\mu$, write $\lambda\mu$ for their concatenation, and write $\trianglerighteq$ for the dominance order induced by the non-increasing rearrangements. **Combinatorial injection conjecture.** There is an injection

$$
\gamma: \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a \hookrightarrow \mathcal{U}^A_a \times \mathcal{U}^B_b
$$

such that, for every $(\lambda_1,\mu_1) \in \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a$, if $(\lambda_2,\mu_2)=\gamma((\lambda_1,\mu_1))$, then

$$
\lambda_1\mu_1 \trianglerighteq \lambda_2\mu_2.
$$

This conjecture gives a combinatorial formulation implying the case $k=2$ of the paper's theorem relating total nonnegativity of the matrices $\mathcal{T}_p$ and $\mathcal{S}_p$.

records.title: Common-basis conjecture for partitions of a matroid ground set
records.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$ on a ground set $E$ with $|E|=kr+1$. Suppose $x,y\in E$ are such that both $E\setminus\{x\}$ and $E\setminus\{y\}$ can be partitioned into $k$ pairwise disjoint bases.

**Common-basis conjecture.** There exist partitions of $E\setminus\{x\}$ and $E\setminus\{y\}$ into $k$ pairwise disjoint bases that share a common basis.

This is the second conjecture introduced as closely related to White's conjectures. It expresses a common-basis condition for two complementary decompositions and is not resolved in the supplied text.

records.title: A fully supported local information maximum on the full two-shift
records.statement: Let $(X,T)$ be the full two-shift, let $\alpha$ be the partition used to define information, and consider the space of one-step Markov measures on $X$. A measure is fully supported when every allowed cylinder has positive measure, and a local maximum is understood relative to this space. **Fully supported local-maximum conjecture.** There is a fully supported one-step Markov measure that is a local maximum of $\operatorname{Int}_\mu(X,T,\alpha)$ among all one-step Markov measures. The assertion is suggested by numerical computations in the source; no proof or resolution is supplied.

records.title: The two-round minimal percolating set conjecture
records.statement:
Let $\Pi_q$ be a finite projective plane of order $q$, let $r$ be the infection rate, and let $t_r(A)$ denote the percolation time of a percolating set $A$. **Two-round minimal percolating set conjecture.** For each $r$ with

$$
4\leq r\leq q,
$$

there exists a minimal percolating set $A_r$ with

$$
t_r(A_r)=2.
$$

This asserts the existence of minimal percolating configurations that infect the entire plane in exactly two rounds throughout the stated range. The source gives a construction and proof around the conjecture, but the supplied parser status is unresolved.

records.title: The expressivity hierarchy conjecture for finitely iterated supervenience languages
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$ be the propositional language with the $n$-ary supervenience operator $\Rrightarrow^n$.

**Expressivity hierarchy conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^{n+1}}$ is more expressive than $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$.

The paper establishes the corresponding result for $n=0$ and leaves the generalization to future work.

records.title: Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture for singular io-decomposable Riordan graphs
records.statement:
Let $G_n(g,zg)$ be a singular io-decomposable Riordan graph, let ${\cal A}_n$ be its adjacency matrix, and let $X=[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]^T$ be an eigenvector with eigenvalue $0$. Define the odd-index and even-index subvectors by

$$
X_o=[x_1,x_3,\ldots,x_{2\lceil n/2\rceil-1}]^T,
$$

$$
X_e=[x_2,x_4,\ldots,x_{2\lfloor n/2\rfloor}]^T.
$$

**Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture.** Then

$$
X_o=O_{\lceil n/2\rceil}.
$$

This claim is motivated by Sage computations and, together with the preceding block-matrix lemma, would constrain the zero-eigenspace of every singular io-decomposable Riordan graph. No proof or resolution is supplied.

records.title: Conjecture on recurrent component cardinalities in sinkless rotor networks
records.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the bidirected cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i}$ denote the unique recurrent component of level $m$ and weight $i\in\mathbb{Z}_n$. Write $r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})$ for the number of recurrent configurations in this component.

**Recurrent-component cardinality conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$, $m\geq 1$, and $i,j\in\mathbb{Z}_n$, one has

$$
r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})=r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,j})
$$

whenever

$$
\gcd(n,m,i)=\gcd(n,m,j).
$$

The conjecture refines the observed near equality of recurrent-component sizes in sinkless rotor networks on bidirected cycles. It is supported by data for small values of $m$ and $n$, but the supplied source does not state a resolution.

records.title: The even-order M{"o}bius ladder local antimagic chromatic number conjecture
records.statement:
For $n\ge 2$, let $M_{2n}$ be the M{"o}bius ladder obtained from the cycle $C_{2n}=u_1u_2\cdots u_nv_1v_2\cdots v_nu_1$ by adding the edges $u_iv_i$ for $1\le i\le n$. Let $\chi_{la}$ denote the local antimagic chromatic number.

**M{"o}bius ladder conjecture.** For even $n\ge 4$,

$$
\chi_{la}(M_{2n})=4.
$$

The surrounding results establish the value for odd $n\ge 3$ and note that $M_4=K_4$ has local antimagic chromatic number $4$. The even-order case stated here is presented as a conjecture, with no resolution supplied in the text.

records.title: Submodular separation conjecture for low-degree monomial families
records.statement:
Let $0\leqslant r\leqslant d$ be integers and let $n=\binom{d}{\leqslant r}$. Define

$$
\phi:\{0,1\}^d\to\{0,1\}^n,
\qquad \phi(x)=\left(\prod_{i\in S}x_i\right)_{S\subset[d]:|S|\leqslant r},
$$

and let ${\mathcal F}_{r,d}=\phi(\{0,1\}^d)$. A function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb Z$ is **submodular** if $f(x)+f(y)\geqslant f(x\vee y)+f(x\wedge y)$ for all $x,y$.

**Submodular separation conjecture.** For every such $r,d$, there exists a submodular function $f$ such that $f(x)$ is computable in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time, $f(x)\leqslant-1$ for every $x\in\mathcal F_{r,d}$, and $f(x)\geqslant0$ for every $x\notin\mathcal F_{r,d}$. If true, this would yield a hardness result for submodular minimization with modular constraints, complementing the known prime-power algorithms; the source does not resolve the conjecture.

records.title: The 2-adic valuation conjecture for even-colored 2-ary partition functions
records.statement:
Let $c_m(n)$ denote the $m$-colored binary partition function, and let $
u_2$ be the 2-adic valuation. For positive integers $k,n$ and nonnegative integers $k$ as specified below, consider the differences of the values of $c_m$. **2-adic valuation conjecture.** For $kin\mathbb{N}_{+}$ and each $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{2k}(4n)-c_{2k}(n))=\nu_{2}(n)+2\nu_{2}(k)+3.
$$
 Moreover, for $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+1}(4n)-c_{4k+1}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+3,
$$
 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+3}(4n)-c_{4k+3}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+6.
$$
 In each case, equality holds for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$. These predictions are motivated by known sharp congruences for the ordinary binary partition function and numerical computations for $m\leq10$ and $n\leq10^5$; their general validity remains open.

records.title: The edge-pattern convex-combination conjecture
records.statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-regular edge-rooted pattern of depth $r$ and girth $2r+2$. For each edge-rooted pattern, let $\mathbf{e}(P)$ denote its constraint vector, and let $\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ be the specified family of $d$-regular edge-rooted trees of depth $r$. The constraint $\mathbf{e}(P)$ is **weaker** than a convex combination of constraints from this family in the sense that there exist $T_1,\dots,T_m\in\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in[0,1]$ with

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1
$$

and, for every $\bm{\alpha}\in{\left(\mathbb{Q}^+\right)}^{r+1}$,

$$
\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\mathbf{e}(T_i)\right)\ge 1\quad\implies\quad\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\mathbf{e}(P)\ge 1.
$$

This would explain why the bounds obtained from edge-rooted trees remain valid at girth $2r+2$, and would generalize the cases checked for $r=2$ and $d\in\{3,4\}$.

records.title: Equitable partitions of rectangular grid graphs
records.statement:
Let $P_m\oblong P_n$ be the rectangular grid graph, and let its automorphism group act naturally on its vertices. An equitable partition is a partition in which every vertex in a cell has the same number of neighbors in each cell.

**Grid-graph equitable-partition conjecture.** The equitable partitions of $P_m\oblong P_n$ are the orbit partitions of natural actions of the subgroups of the automorphism group of the graph. The lattice of equitable partitions is isomorphic to the lattice of subgroups exactly when there is a vertex with trivial stabilizer subgroup. This happens unless $2\le m=n\le3$.

The claim concerns the relationship between equitable partitions and symmetry-induced orbit partitions for rectangular grid graphs. The supplied text reports this as an apparent pattern based on computations, but gives no resolution or proof.

records.title: Uniqueness of code-loop representations by degree and type
records.statement: Let $L$ be a code loop, and let $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ be representations of $L$. The **degree-and-type uniqueness conjecture.** If $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ have the same degree and type, then they are isomorphic. The claim is motivated by the fact that, for code loops of ranks 3 and 4, the type determines the loop up to isomorphism; whether the analogous uniqueness holds in general is left open.

records.title: The growth constant for the stack-sorting map
records.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $s:S_n\to S_n$ be the stack-sorting map, and let $\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)$ denote its maximum fiber size. The paper considers the exponential growth rate

$$
\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)^{1/n}.
$$

**Stack-sorting growth conjecture.** The value of this limit lies in the interval $(1.68,1.73)$.

The interval is suggested by computations on random permutations for $n=100$ and $n=300$. The problem of obtaining improved asymptotic estimates, or exact formulas, remains open.

records.title: The rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture
records.statement:
Let $G$ and $\overline{G}$ be nontrivial connected graphs of order $n\geq 8$. Write $rvd(G)$ for the rainbow vertex-disconnection number of $G$. **Rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture.**

$$
rvd(G)+rvd(\overline{G})\geq n.
$$

This conjecture proposes an improvement of the established lower bound for the sum of the rainbow vertex-disconnection numbers of a graph and its complement. The paper notes that the bound holds when $rvd(G)=1$, but does not establish it for all nontrivial connected graphs of order at least $8$.

records.title: The kernel conjecture for the second-kind interval transform
records.statement:
Let ${\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$ denote the vector space of homogeneous noncommutative $ab$-polynomials of degree $n$, and let $I_2:{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n\rightarrow {\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_{n+1}$ be the interval transform of the second kind. Let $A_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$ be the specified subspace of ${\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$. 

**Kernel conjecture.** For each $n\geq 1$, 

$$
\ker I_2=A_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n.
$$

The conjecture identifies precisely the kernel of the second-kind interval transform, whose nontrivial kernel distinguishes it from the corresponding Tchebyshev operator framework. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

records.title: Latin-strategy characterization conjecture for the symmetric group
records.statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **Latin strategy** is obtained by choosing an $n\times n$ Latin square $S$; Alice's message identifies a row of $S$ that agrees with the input permutation at the maximum possible number of positions. An optimal strategy is one attaining the maximum success probability.

**Latin-strategy characterization conjecture.** Optimal strategies are exactly Latin strategies.

This conjecture proposes a complete characterization of optimal strategies, extending the explicitly described shift strategies. The paper states it as an open question and does not prove the characterization.

records.title: Nonexistence conjecture for dendrimer nanostars of at least four stages
records.statement: A **dendrimer nanostar** is the nanostar structure obtained by growing a dendrimer through a specified number of stages; a graph is a **$G_\phi$-graph** if it is realized as $G_\phi(A)$ for an appropriate set $A$, using the Euler $\phi$ function as in the paper. **Nonexistence conjecture for dendrimer nanostars.** There is no dendrimer nanostar which has grown at least four stages, as a $G_\phi$-graph. The paper proves that the two-stage nanostar $D_2$ is a $G_\phi$-graph, while reporting that attempts to prove nonexistence for nanostars grown through at least four stages have failed; the conjecture remains open.

records.title: Estrada–Mugnolo's Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture for hubs-biased resistance distances
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-repelling resistance distance, $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)$ for the standard Kirchhoff index, and $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-attracting resistance distance.

**Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture.** For $\alpha\in\{-1,1\}$,

$$
\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G),
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is regular.

The conjecture was formulated after computational experiments on more than 12,000 connected graphs with $5\leq n\leq 8$, and predicts that hubs-repelling navigation gives the largest Kirchhoff index while hubs-attracting navigation gives the smallest. Its general validity is left open in the source.

records.title: Non-IR conjecture for paths and cycles
records.statement:
Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and $C_n$ the cycle on $n$ vertices. An **IR-graph** is a graph arising as an irredundance graph.

**Non-IR conjecture for paths and cycles.** The path $P_n$ is not an IR-graph for each $n\geq 3$, and the cycle $C_n$ is not an IR-graph for each $n\geq 5$.

These are open problems concerning which graphs can occur as irredundance graphs. They are stated together in the paper's list of conjectures and open problems and are attributed there to Mynhardt (2019).

records.title: Signed cycle-type restriction polynomiality conjecture
records.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $k$ be a fixed positive integer with $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ elements. For $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, let $\operatorname{type}(\pi)$ be its cycle type, and let $\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)$ denote its right-to-left-minimum-value and excedance-value multisets, respectively. Then **the polynomiality conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\min(\operatorname{type}(\pi))\geq k}}(-1)^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}\mathbf{x}_{\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)}\mathbf{y}_{\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)}
$$

is an element of $\mathbb{N}[x_1,\dotsc,x_n,y_1,\dotsc,y_n]$. This generalizes the derangement case by imposing a lower bound on the lengths of all cycles; the source provides no resolution or further evidence for the claim, so its status remains open.

records.title: Circulant graph conjecture for monophonic position number two
records.statement: Let $n$ be an integer, and let a **circulant graph** mean a graph whose vertices are arranged cyclically with adjacency determined by a fixed set of cyclic differences. The monophonic position number is denoted by $a$, and the diameter by $D$. **Circulant graph conjecture.** For any $n\geq 11$, there is a circulant graph with order $n$, monophonic position number $a=2$, and diameter $D=2$. The preceding theorem establishes existence of some graph with these parameters if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,8\}$ or $n\geq 11$; the conjecture strengthens the large-order existence assertion by requiring the graph to be circulant, based on computational evidence.

records.title: Subgraph criterion for minimal doubled 3-regular graphs
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a doubled 3-regular graph. Perform the YY-$\Delta$ transformation on all wyes in all possible ways to obtain a graph $G'$ of smallest size. A **chain of 3-cycles** is a chain of one or more 3-cycles, each connected by a vertex that is also doubly adjacent to one more vertex, with the 3-cycles at either end having one vertex with exactly 4 neighbours and no connections of size greater than 2.

**Minimality criterion conjecture.** The graph $G'$ is a minimal graph if and only if it does not contain such a chain of 3-cycles.

The conjecture proposes that, for doubled 3-regular graphs, checking the more restricted subgraphs illustrated in the first column of the paper's figure suffices to determine minimality. The source gives examples and discusses related reducible subgraphs, but provides no proof or resolution.

records.title: The Polynexus formula for nonzero products in the rook monoid
records.statement:
Let $M_n$ be the monoid of rook diagrams and let $\mathbf{0}$ denote its zero element. Let $\psi(n)$ be the number of nonzero products arising from $M_n\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}$.

**Polynexus conjecture.** For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\psi(n)$ equals the $(n+1)$th Polynexus number of order $7$, namely

$$
\psi(n)=\frac{(n+1)^7-n^7-(n+1)^3+n^3}{120}.
$$

The formula was suggested by numerical evaluation of the sextuple sum defining $\psi(n)$ and comparison with the Polynexus numbers. An analytic evaluation of that sum was not available in the source, so the conjecture remains open here.

records.title: Unit-gap conjecture for diameters of Schrijver graphs
records.statement:
Let $k$ and $r$ be integers with $2\leq r\leq k-2$, and let $D(G)$ denote the diameter of a graph $G$. For $n=2k+r$, write $\operatorname{SG}(n,k)$ for the Schrijver graph. **Unit-gap conjecture.** If $2\leq r\leq k-2$, then

$$
D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r,k)\right)-D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r+1,k)\right)\in\\{0,1\\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the possibility of larger drops in the diameter as $r$ increases. It is based on computations and is open; the paper notes that the analogous differences are in $\\{0,1\\}$ for $k\leq 5$, while a larger gap occurs at the transition from $r=1$ to $r=2$ when $k\geq 6$.

records.title: Balanced-graph conjecture for flat graphs
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a flat graph, and let $c_i(G)$ denote the number of $i$-cliques in $G$. Define

$$
D_{clique}(G)=\left|\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ odd}}c_i(G)-\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ even}}c_i(G)\right|.
$$

Call $G$ **balanced** when $D_{clique}(G)\leq 1$.

**Balanced-graph conjecture.** Any flat graph is a balanced graph.

The source notes that related subclasses of flat graphs satisfy $D_{clique}(G)=1$. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture, so it remains open.

records.title: Uniqueness conjecture for power domination reconfiguration graphs of complete bipartite graphs
records.statement: Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $s$ and $t$, and let $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ denote its power domination reconfiguration graph under token addition/removal reconfiguration. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ is unique if and only if $s\ne 2$ and $t\ne 2$. This is supported by the uniqueness results for $K_{1,t}$ with $t\ge 3$ and $K_{3,3}$, together with Sage computations for $s\in\{3,4\}$ and $t\in\{3,4,5\}$; the conjecture proposes the complete characterization, including the cases not covered by those results.

records.title: Even-arity complete full tree local antimagic chromatic number conjecture
records.statement:
Let $T$ be a complete full $t$-ary tree, meaning a rooted tree in which every nonleaf has exactly $t$ children and all leaves have the same depth. Let $l$ be the number of leaves and let $\chi_{la}(T)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number. **Even-arity complete full tree conjecture.** For every even integer $t\geq2$,

$$
\chi_{la}(T)=l+1.
$$

The paper explicitly states this conjecture as open; it would sharpen the established upper bound $\chi_{la}(T)\leq l+2$, while the equality is proved in the paper for odd $t$.

records.title: Improved upper bounds for Staller–Maker–Breaker domination numbers
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$. The S-game and D-game parameters are denoted by $\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)$ and $\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)$, respectively.

**Improved SMBD-number bounds.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)\le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-\delta(G)+1;\\
&\text{(ii) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-\delta(G)+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds would improve the known sharp general upper bounds when the minimum degree is at least two; the authors note that sharp examples under this degree condition are not known.

records.title: Strict middle-graph increase conjecture for outer-connected domination
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$. The **strict middle-graph increase conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(G) < \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The paper notes that this inequality holds for trees and for several standard graph families, including complete graphs, wheels, friendship graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and cycles. Whether it holds for every graph of order at least two remains open.

records.title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
records.statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.

records.title: Hurlbert's ordering conjecture for universal cycles of permutations
records.statement: Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{O}(n)$ be the clustered graph of overlapping $n$-permutations: its edges are the permutations in $S_n$, and consecutive permutations overlap in their last and first $n-1$ entries up to reduction. **Hurlbert's ordering conjecture.** Given any Euler tour of the clustered graph of overlapping permutations (that is, an ordering of $S_n$ such that each consecutive pair of permutations overlaps), there is a universal cycle for permutations that covers $S_n$ in the same order. Universal cycles correspond to Euler tours in this graph, but it remains open whether every such ordering can be realized by a universal cycle.

records.title: The prime-modulus conjecture for progression-free digit sets
records.statement:
Let $p\geq 13$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\bmod 4$, and let $n$ be an integer divisible by $(p+3)/2$. For a digit set $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$, write $S(D,n)$ for the set of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ in which every digit of $D$ occurs the same number of times. Define

$$
D=\left\{0,1,\ldots,\frac{p-1}{2},\frac{p+3}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Prime-modulus progression-free-set conjecture.** The set $S(D,n)$ does not contain any arithmetic progression of length $4$.

This conjecture extends the progression-free constructions for odd progression lengths to a case not covered by the stated theorem, motivated by computations with small primes. Its status is unresolved in the source.

records.title: Linear-bound multiset reconstruction conjecture for tableau minors
records.statement: Let $k\geq 1$ and let $T\in\operatorname{YT}(n)$, where $n\geq k+4$. Here $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ denotes the multiset of $k$-minors of the standard Young tableau $T$. **Multiset reconstruction conjecture.** The multiset $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ determines $T$. This proposed linear bound is supported by computer verification for $k\leq 5$, and concerns reconstructibility from multisets of $k$-minors.

records.title: The GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture for exact slow NIM
records.statement: Consider the exact slow game NIM$(n,n-1)$ for $\ell$ players: a position is a non-negative $n$-vector, players move cyclically, and on each move a player keeps one entry unchanged and decreases each of the other $n-1$ positive entries by $1$. A position with at least two non-positive entries is terminal; the player whose turn it is loses, and the other $\ell-1$ players share the payoff $\frac{C-L(P)}{\ell-1}$, where $L(P)$ is the play length and $C$ exceeds the length of every play from the initial position. The GM-rule specifies a strategy for each player, including the move that keeps the largest entry when no entry is a multiple of $\ell$. **GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture.** The set of $\ell$ GM-strategies forms a uniform Nash equilibrium. The claim concerns the strategic behavior induced by the GM-rule in the multiplayer exact slow NIM game; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

records.title: Intermediate-value conjecture for orientable total domination numbers
records.statement:
Let $G\in\mathcal{C}$ be a graph, and let ${\rm dom}_t(G)$ and ${\rm DOM}_t(G)$ denote its lower and upper orientable total domination numbers. For an orientation $f$ of $G$, write $G_f$ for the resulting oriented graph and $\gamma_t(G_f)$ for its total domination number. **Intermediate-value conjecture.** For every integer $c$ satisfying

$$
{\rm dom}_t(G)\leq c\leq {\rm DOM}_t(G),
$$

there exists an orientation $f$ of $G$ such that

$$
\gamma_t(G_f)=c.
$$

This extends the corresponding result known for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs. The source attributes the conjecture to the authors of the cited earlier work, and no resolution is given here.

records.title: The set-palette conjecture for complete graphs
records.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In a general edge-coloring of $K_n$, let $\tau_s(n)$ denote the minimum number of colors needed so that all triangles have distinct color palettes when a palette is viewed as the set of colors appearing on its three edges. **Set-palette conjecture.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\tau_s(n)=n-1.
$$

The source notes the inequality $\tau_m(n)\leq\tau_s(n)\leq\tau'(n)$ and states that this conjecture would imply the preceding multiset-palette conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

records.title: Largest rigid facet conjecture for Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes
records.statement:
Let $Q_n=\\{\pm1\\}^n$ be the Hamming cube with Hamming distance. A subset is **maximally diameter-$r$** if its diameter is $r$ and adjoining any point outside it produces diameter greater than $r$; it is **rigid** if every point has a point at distance equal to the diameter. Let $b'(n;r)$ be the size of the largest maximally diameter-$r$, rigid subset of $Q_n$, equivalently the largest such rigid facet in $\operatorname{\mathcal{VR}}(Q_n;r)$. **Largest rigid facet conjecture.**

$$
b'(n;r)=2^r
$$

whenever $n\geq r$. The subcube $Q_r\times\\{\mathbf 1_{n-r}\\}$ supplies an extremal candidate of size $2^r$, but the conjectured upper bound is not proved in the source.

records.title: Contact-order distance conjecture for colored graph representations
records.statement: Let $G$ be a graph whose vertices are colored with $z$ and $w$, and let $i$ be a vertex from which the representation is computed. The **contact order** is the order describing how the associated level curves approach one another near a boundary singularity. **Contact-order distance conjecture.** The contact order of the representation computed from vertex $i$ is twice the path distance from $i$ to the closest vertex colored $w$. The source reports computational evidence for this extension, but does not state a proof or resolution.

records.title: The local antimagic chromatic number conjecture for joins of matching and null graphs
records.statement:
Let $r,s\ge 1$ and $m\ge 2$. For a graph $G$, its **local antimagic chromatic number** $\chi_{la}(G)$ is the least number of distinct induced vertex labels among bijective local antimagic edge labelings of $G$. Let $(2s+1)P_2$ be the disjoint union of $2s+1$ copies of the two-vertex path, let $O_m$ be the null graph on $m$ vertices, let $\vee$ denote the graph join, and let $2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)$ be the disjoint union of $2r$ copies of this join.

**Local antimagic chromatic number conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{la}\bigl(2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)\bigr)=3.
$$

This is posed as an open problem in the conclusion, extending results on local antimagic chromatic numbers for joins of special graph families. The claim predicts a constant value of $3$ throughout the stated parameter range.

records.title: Maximum sigma_t-irregularity conjecture for connected triangle-free graphs
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. Write $sigma_t(G)$ for its $sigma_t$-irregularity. Among such graphs, the extremal complete bipartite graphs are conjectured to have maximum $sigma_t(G)$.

**Triangle-free extremal conjecture.** Among connected triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the extremal complete bipartite graphs have the maximum $sigma_t(G)$-irregularity.

The paper proves the corresponding extremal result among complete bipartite graphs and proposes this conjecture as the extension to all connected triangle-free graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

records.title: Nonexistence conjecture for cubic 8-circulant nut graphs
records.statement: A **cubic $8$-circulant nut graph** is a cubic nut graph admitting an $8$-circulant structure. **Nonexistence conjecture for cubic $8$-circulant nut graphs.** There exists no cubic $8$-circulant nut graph. This is the only unresolved case in the cubic $\ell$-circulant nut graph existence problem; computational results suggest that such graphs might not exist, but no proof is given here.

records.title: The majorization characterization conjecture for ordinal spaces embeddable in the line
records.statement:
Let $(X,\delta)$ be an ordinal space with $|X|=n\in\mathbb N^+$, and let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ be an enumeration of its points satisfying the majorization property. Write $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1$ for embeddability of $X$ in the real line. **Majorization characterization conjecture.** If such an enumeration exists, then

$$
X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1.
$$

The paper proves that line embeddability implies the existence of an enumeration with the majorization property and states sufficiency for $n\leqslant4$, while explicitly saying that it cannot determine whether sufficiency holds for $n>5$; the general assertion is therefore open.

records.title: Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles
records.statement:
Let $C_m$ and $C_n$ be cycles with $m,n\geq3$, and let $\mathrm{pmd}(G)$ denote the positive matching decomposition number. **Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles.**

$$
\mathrm{pmd}(C_m\square C_n)=6
$$

for all $m,n\geq3$ such that $m+n$ is even, or such that $(m,n)\in\{(3,4),(3,6),(5,6)\}$. The supplied text presents this exact-value assertion after an analysis of positive matchings in the relevant Cartesian products; no resolution beyond that analysis is provided.

records.title: The neighborhood-tour conjecture for ASEP vertices
records.statement: Let $P_{\text{ASEP}}^{n}$ be the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope, let $\boldsymbol{x}$ be a vertex of this polytope, and let $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{x})$ denote its neighborhood in the vertex structure considered by the paper. A **tour** is a Hamiltonian cycle of the complete directed graph on the node set. **Neighborhood-tour conjecture.** For every vertex $\boldsymbol{x}$, the neighborhood $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{x})$ contains at least one tour. This is presented as a conjecture based on preliminary computational tests; the supplied text does not establish it or indicate a resolution.

records.title: The representation-number conjecture for larger toroidal grid graphs
records.statement:
Let $\text{TGr}_{m,n}$ be the toroidal grid graph formed from the Cartesian product of the cycle graphs $C_m$ and $C_n$, with $m,n\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote the representation number of a graph $G$. **Representation-number conjecture.** If $n,m\geq 3$ and $m+n\geq 8$, then

$$
\mathcal{R}(\text{TGr}_{m,n})\geq 4.
$$

The graphs $\text{TGr}_{3,3}$ and $\text{TGr}_{3,4}$ have known 3-representations, but no 3-representation is known for larger toroidal grid graphs; the conjecture predicts that all cases with $m+n\geq 8$ require representation number at least $4$.

records.title: Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order
records.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.

records.title: The collapsing conjecture for facets of hierarchical model polytopes
records.statement:
Let $p\leq q\leq r$ be positive integers, and let $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ denote the polytope associated with the hierarchical model in the paper. A facet is **obtained by collapsing** if it arises from a facet of a smaller table through the paper's collapsing operation.

**Collapsing conjecture.** Suppose that

$$
p \leq q \leq r.
$$

Then all facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ are obtained by collapsing from facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,q}$.

The conjecture is motivated by computational results summarized in the paper's table, although the authors also exhibit a non-collapsible facet of $P_\Delta^{4,4,4}$, showing that not every facet arises by collapsing to a binary table. The conjecture remains open in the supplied source.

records.title: The distance bound for loops with nonequivalent associator
records.statement:
Let $L=(G,\circ)$ and $M=(G,*)$ be Moufang loops on the same set $G$ of order $n$, and define their distance by

$$
d(\circ,*)=\left|\{(a,b)\in G\times G: a\circ b\ne a*b\}\right|.
$$
 Suppose that $L$ and $M$ have nonequivalent associators. **Distance-bound conjecture.** Their distance satisfies

$$
d(\circ,*)\ge 3n^2/8.
$$
 This conjecture asks for the minimum distance between Moufang loops with nonequivalent associator; the source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.

records.title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
records.statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

records.title: Conjecture on the super edge-magic total strength of odd-cycle unicyclic graphs
records.statement:
Let $G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n})$ be the super edge-magic total unicyclic $(p,q)$-graph consisting of an odd cycle

$$
C_n=\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n\}
$$

and $k_i$ pendant vertices adjacent to each $a_i$, for $1\leq i\leq n$. Here $s m(G)$ denotes the super edge-magic total strength of $G$. **Super edge-magic total strength conjecture.**

$$
s m(G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n}))=2q+\frac{n+3}{2}.
$$

The claim extends the known exact value for the uniform family $k_i=k$, while the paper presents computations for certain graphs in this broader family as supporting evidence; its general validity remains open.

records.title: Orientation of nonideal clutters
records.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a clutter on ground set V, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be its blocker. Is it true that $\mathcal{C}$ is nonideal if and only if there exist $p:{\mathcal C} \to V$ and $q: {\mathcal B} \to V$ such that $p(X)\in X$ for every $X \in {\mathcal C}$, $p(Y)\in Y$ for every $Y \in {\mathcal B}$, if $p(X)=q(Y)$, then $|X \cap Y|>1$?
